A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RECA research work. All 34 pages of v3 and 43 pages of v4, including equations, tables, figures and appendices, support comparison. Retained material can be matched across appendix renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v3 reports original RECA experiments on image generation, editing and visual understanding, including quantitative comparisons, ablations and qualitative results in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds compositional evaluation, data-scale and data-source experiments, and mechanistic analyses in Appendices D and F.

M1.justification: The reconstruction objective, loss weighting, freezing rules, input-resolution strategy and inference procedure remain unchanged in Section 2. The expanded visual-embedding integration description documents the existing procedure; revised architecture labels do not introduce a method change.

E1.justification: v4 adds T2I-CompBench evaluation covering shape, texture, numeracy, 3D spatial relationships and complex compositions. Appendix F.8 also adds COCO2014 and JourneyDB training-data comparisons, notably extending testing to real-world training images. Existing generation, editing and understanding coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding quantitative and qualitative comparisons. BAGEL-NHR, FLUX-Kontext and ICEdit already appear in v3. The new compositional benchmark reuses the existing Show-o, Harmon, OpenUni and BAGEL baseline/RECA pairs rather than introducing another comparison method.

E3.justification: Table 8 revises reported weight decay from 0.01 to 0.02 for Harmon, 0.05 for OpenUni and 0 for BAGEL. The reported GEdit evaluator changes from gpt-4o-2024-11-20 to gpt-4.1-2025-04-14. New protocols include QwenVL-2.5-32B judging for compositional evaluation and 10,000/50,000/240,000-image scale comparisons. These revisions do not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds layer-wise PCA, semantic-projection cases and paired reconstruction/generation failure analysis. Appendices F.7–F.8 add reconstruction progression, cross-architecture reconstruction comparisons and data-scale/source ablations. Existing leakage, encoder-resolution and training-order analyses remain. The standalone BAGEL distribution-mismatch illustration is removed, although its discussion remains.

E5.justification: Appendix D newly states that the reconstruction failure example persists across multiple random seeds, without specifying their number or quantifying uncertainty. The existing 12-repetition policy using seeds 0–11 and default seed 0 elsewhere is unchanged. No new confidence intervals or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: New Tables 12–14 report substantial additional outcomes, including OpenUni compositional overall scores of 78.84 before RECA and 86.49 afterward, and COCO-trained GenEval performance of 85.3. Existing absolute benchmark scores remain unchanged, but reported gains are corrected: ImgEdit replacement +0.44 to +0.46, GEdit overall +0.37 to +0.33, and Harmon-0.5B counting +1.6 to +3.6. New qualitative results also appear.

T1.justification: Equations 1–14 retain the same mathematical content. The renamed generation paradigms and new empirical discussion of feature isomorphism introduce no formal definitions, assumptions, theorems, proofs or substantive derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same central claims: caption-free reconstruction post-training using existing visual embeddings, broad architectural applicability, and efficient generation/editing improvements. Additional appendix evidence and revised model-family terminology do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix D introduces substantive interpretations involving visual/text feature isomorphism, internal semantic projection and reconstruction as a pathway to generation improvement. Appendix F interprets new results as evidence of depth/occlusion understanding and broader data-distribution applicability. The original counting and BLIP-3o limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 and Figure 10 newly specify the chat-template sequence and visual-embedding integration. Hyperparameter and evaluator documentation is revised, and the added experiments disclose evaluator and dataset-size information. Existing hardware, training-time information and the promise to release code and weights remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds references for the new benchmark, datasets and analyses, plus recent work such as UniCTokens, SRUM and Echo-4o. Section 4 modestly updates post-training coverage. The central positioning against ViLex, ROSS, REPA and Lumos in Section 2.3 remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Local edits clarify generation-family terminology as discrete, MAR and continuous, expand and subdivide the prompt appendix, and reorganize appendices around the new mechanistic section. The main narrative remains largely intact. Conference headers and affiliation information are updated, and acknowledgments are removed.

P2.justification: v4 substantially expands the appendix displays with an input-format diagram, PCA and semantic case figures, reconstruction panels, three quantitative tables and four additional generation grids. These are substantive visual additions beyond renumbering. Most earlier displays are retained, while v3's distribution-mismatch Figure 10 is removed.

improvement.justification: Beyond v3's already extensive evaluation, v4 adds useful compositional and real-world/data-scale evidence in Tables 12–14 and clearer input documentation. These strengthen support for generality. The gains are moderated by mechanistic claims that exceed the illustrative evidence, an unexplained mapping from ten stated benchmark dimensions to eight tabulated categories, and protocol revisions whose relationship to unchanged headline scores is unclear.
